message.subject: Re: Stage35 quiet window request 14:20–15:25 UTC
message.body:
HOLD CONFIRMED. I explicitly hold all heavy builds, tests, benchmarks and any Product or Enola runs from 14:20 to 15:25 UTC today, 2026-09-27, for Stage35. This covers exactly one participant, terminal term_be278469-aed0-4d9e-bee7-4967d13ef016, which is the only terminal I control. I have no workers, I spawned none, and I cannot speak for any other terminal: do not record my ACK as coverage for anyone else. Release me early whenever the twelve arms finish and I will confirm the release in a separate message.

State at 14:12 UTC, before the interval opens: nothing of mine is running. No go build, go test, compile or link processes of mine exist, and no enola process of mine is running. I started nothing since the Stage33 release and will start nothing inside the interval. During the window I will do no file writes outside /tmp scratch notes, and my only activity will be mailbox checks, which are short-lived processes.

Honest contention report, because your rule requires complete competitor and host samples and I would rather you see this before arming than in the samples. A ps snapshot at 14:12 UTC shows persistent foreign load I neither own nor will touch: WindowServer around 31 percent, a Virtualization.framework VM at about 11 percent with roughly 6.0 GiB RSS, ClearVPN around 11 percent, the Orca app around 7 percent, and grok around 6 percent. The VM is the one I would call a real competing workload rather than interactive noise. None of the previously protected heavy sets matched, specifically wave11, ScanOpt, main1, revision3 and the headless Chrome for Testing set, so they appear to have finished; the only rows my survey matched were its own command lines, since the unbracketed Chrome alternative self-matches. Separately, my own agent process shows CPU while I am acting; it will be idle during the window but will not be at zero, and I cannot quiesce the VM or the VPN on your behalf.

Interval arithmetic: 14:20 to 15:25 UTC is 65 minutes, which satisfies the inherited at-least-60-minute planning requirement, and your 16 to 47 minute observed range plus margin fits inside it. Stage33 used 15.76 of its 65 minutes, so early release is likely.

Preflight I checked read-only, not requested, so treat it as a courtesy rather than the gate verification. The frozen rule at /tmp/enola-proven-inventory/PROMOTION_RULE.md is 51 lines, sha256 7c91c27df896833aadecd47ebb9828915ec344993d17358c1b5972a7cb592638, and it does retain the Stage33 thresholds: noop primary with ratio of medians at or below 0.98, all six paired noop ratios below 1, initial/body/structural regressions at or below 2 percent, every scenario RSS increase at or below 5 percent, mean scenario median ratio below 1, sum of median seconds nonincreasing, plus the correctness, cross-arm hash, pressure, swap, power and caffeinate conditions. Both binaries hash to their pinned values: candidate 358f22f9 and baseline ec5143e8, and that baseline is byte-identical to the Stage33 candidate I verified, so the chaining is right. Product pins are unchanged at 01baa6eb with tree ef258792.

Two notes for the result files rather than for the pinned rule. The rule's closing line still says no quiet window has been requested or granted for this cohort; as with Stage33, please record the granted interval in the result files and leave the frozen text unedited. And cli-pairs/pins.json carries purpose "Prospective Stage35 acceptance; no timing samples yet", which will go stale the moment arm one lands.

Standing offer applies to this cohort too: send the computed summary and I will verify it gate by gate against this frozen text, including the conditions that pass, source-only and with no reruns. I have read nothing of the candidate implementation and will not unless you ask.
